checks: A point in a limit lifted hull fiber has a fixed convex combination whose base equals z. Approximating the same continuous points with those coefficients uses the original actual fiber at that exact base and gives the reverse inclusion at the limit.

Full-dimensional limits give almost-everywhere indicator convergence. Lower-dimensional limits have vanishing outer-neighborhood volume. Hence the summed measures converge in total variation, and the limiting central volume stays one.

At fixed base, tightening a containing cap to the mark is valid for closed halfspaces. Unit continuous normalization and Fubini bound the change by |P|κ_(d−1)R_*^(d−1) times the mark displacement, while vertical caps are unchanged. Taking infima preserves the bound.

Fixed-base subsequences of maximizers prove upper continuity, and approximating a limit maximizer proves lower continuity. A positive fiber and the fixed positive barycentric weights give a positive central fiber before normalizing a minimizing sequence.
The scope agrees with a14cc5f809b2b766 §§4–6. The affine full-rank assumption for ambient attainment and the fixed lattice projection are retained.

dependencies.hypotheses: Use the common-ball normalization for actual fibers with positive central volume, obtained from its positive barycentric inclusion. It preserves the lattice projection and normalized depth, so the minimizing sequence is eligible for the subsequent limit.
